revisions.content:
## Investment thesis
Aster makes the components that turn computing demand into physical infrastructure. The question is whether its expanding order book can become durable cash flow without an equally large increase in capital requirements.

Our working view is constructive on the business, cautious on the assumptions. Demand alone does not establish an attractive investment. The analysis needs a defensible margin of safety and a clearer picture of customer concentration.

## Business quality
The fictional business supplies specialized networking components to data-center operators. Its position rests on qualification cycles, integration expertise, and switching costs rather than a consumer brand.

The strongest part of the case is repeat design wins. The weakest is the assumption that today's infrastructure build-out continues at the same pace.

## Financial performance
Illustrative figures only. USD millions; fiscal years are example periods.

| Metric | FY2024 | FY2025 | Change |
| Revenue | 2,400 | 3,120 | +30.0% |
| Operating profit | 480 | 718 | +49.6% |
| Free cash flow | 310 | 425 | +37.1% |
| Operating margin | 20.0% | 23.0% | +3.0 pts |

Revenue growth and operating leverage move together in this example. Free cash flow grows more slowly than operating profit, making working capital the next item to investigate.

## Valuation
No price target is established. Build downside, base, and upside cases using normalized margins and reinvestment needs. The current share price and fully diluted share count have not been supplied.

## Risks
- Customer concentration can turn one delayed order into a material earnings revision.
- Capacity investments may precede demand by several quarters.
- Competitors may reduce the premium earned on specialized designs.

## Open questions
- How much of the order book is cancellable?
- What explains the gap between profit and cash conversion?
- What happens to returns on capital at a lower utilization rate?

## Sources
This is a fictional demonstration report. No external filings or verified market data were used.
